To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) adaptive security in threshold settings is a very challenging problem, and (ii) we have developed the first threshold signature schemes with adaptive security, and the first threshold cryptosystems with adaptive security in the threshold setting.

(a) a new adaptive threshold signature scheme is presented that is based on a threshold cryptosystem and that provides a high level of security; (b) the security of this signature scheme has been proven; and (c) this signature scheme is more efficient than other signature schemes that provide the same security level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (1) Threshold Cryptosystems and Signature Schemes.
the design and implementation of cryptographic protocols and systems.
designing, analyzing, and implementing cryptographic protocols for secure computation and secure data storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of threshold cryptography is not yet mature and requires further research.
the security of threshold cryptosystems and schemes is determined by the underlying single-server systems.

the security of threshold cryptosystems is not as high as the security of single-server cryptosystems, and that this is a consequence of the fact that threshold schemes are more complex and therefore more vulnerable to attack than single-server systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach for the design of threshold schemes.
we have shown how to design a threshold signature scheme from a standard single-user scheme.
we have designed the most efficient threshold cryptosystem and signature schemes in terms of the number of bits communicated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of threshold protocols can be adapted to the setting of the threshold.
, when designing threshold systems, one must be very careful to take into account the security properties of the single-server systems used as building blocks.
the security of threshold protocols is often much more fragile than that of the underlying single-server systems.
